newsitem.title: GERMANY: German stocks start bourse dealing off records.
newsitem.headline: German stocks start bourse dealing off records.

text.p: German shares opened bourse dealings on Wednesday lower, discouraged by weakness on foreign markets, but supported by strength in the German bond market.
Dealers said they expected the DAX index of 30 leading shares to hold around 2,800 points, the psychological and technical level it managed to penetrate decisively for the first time on Tuesday.
The DAX index was down 9.09 points, or 0.32 percent, at 2,801.55 points by 1030 GMT, hovering just above the crucial 2,800 point level.
German Bund strength had been supportive for the market in early dealings as the December Bund future made an all-time high of 101.55. But the contract later pared gains to around 101.42.

Shares in Europe's largest carmaker Volkswagen were in the spotlight, slipping almost five percent, or 29.50 marks to 609.50 marks by 1030 GMT, after a U.S. judge denied VW's motion to dismiss racketeering claims by rival Opel.
The ruling could open VW to potentially higher damages in the lawsuit with the subsidiary of U.S. carmaker General Motors.
VW shares were also under pressure after the firm said it could introduce short-time working hours at its main plant because a French truck blockade has hit the supply of car parts.
Shares in other carmakers were also weaker than the trend, BMW down nine marks at 976 marks and Daimler-Benz AG off 78 pfennigs at 99.10 marks.
Meanwhile shares in newly-floated Deutsche Telekom were stronger than the market trend, gaining 16 pfennigs to 33.16 marks.
Shares in diversified group Veba AG were also firmer, rising 33 pfennigs to 89 marks after the group said it plans to create 15,000 jobs in the coming year, mainly in its telecommunications division.
Veba's chief executive Ulrich Hartmann also said Deutsche Telekom would remain relevant in its relevant sectors for decades to come.
